title: Pharmacist Salary Australia: Award Rates, Casual Loading, and Super Paid on Top
description: Learn how to calculate a pharmacist salary Australia using Fair Work award rates. Includes hourly to annual conversion, casual loading, superannuation, and tax estimates.
salarySummary: A full-time pharmacist under the Pharmacy Industry Award earns a minimum hourly rate of $41.74, equating to about $82,478 per year for 38 hours per week, with superannuation paid on top.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for a pharmacist in Australia?
faqs.a: Under the Pharmacy Industry Award 2020, the minimum hourly rate for a pharmacist is $41.74 per hour for full-time or part-time employees. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top, making the casual rate $52.18 per hour (inclusive of the loading). These rates apply from the first full pay period on or after 1 July 2026.

faqs.q: How is casual loading calculated for a pharmacist?
faqs.a: Casual loading is 25% of the minimum hourly rate. For a pharmacist, the base rate is $41.74, so the casual loading adds $10.44, resulting in a casual rate of $52.18 per hour. This loading is paid for all ordinary hours and is included in the casual penalty rates shown in the award. Superannuation is then calculated on the ordinary earnings, not including the loading.

faqs.q: Does superannuation count as part of my pharmacist salary?
faqs.a: No, superannuation is paid on top of your salary. Under the award, employers must contribute at least 12% of your ordinary earnings (up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year) to a super fund. For a full-time pharmacist earning $82,478 per year, the super contribution would be about $9,897, bringing total remuneration to around $92,375.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Pharmacist Salary Australia Landscape

When researching a **pharmacist salary Australia**, the most reliable source is the Fair Work Ombudsman’s Pharmacy Industry Award 2020. This award sets minimum pay rates for all pharmacy employees, from assistants to pharmacists. For a qualified pharmacist, the minimum hourly rate from 1 July 2026 is **$41.74 per hour** for full-time and part-time employees. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making their minimum **$52.18 per hour**.

The award also defines higher classifications: an experienced pharmacist ($45.72/hr), pharmacist in charge ($46.80/hr), and pharmacist manager ($52.15/hr). These rates are the legal minimum; many employers pay above award, but the award provides the baseline for calculating annual pay, casual loading, and superannuation.

## Converting Hourly to Annual Pay

To estimate your annual gross pay, use the formula:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time pharmacist working 38 ordinary hours per week (the standard under the award), the calculation is:

$41.74 × 38 × 52 = **$82,478.24 per year**

If you are paid fortnightly, multiply the weekly rate by 2: $41.74 × 38 × 2 = **$3,172.24 per fortnight**. This is before tax and any deductions.

This formula assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For a more personalised estimate, use [the timesheet](/) to enter your base hourly rate and toggle casual loading.

## Casual Loading and Superannuation Paid on Top

### Casual Loading

Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on the minimum hourly rate. This compensates for the lack of paid leave entitlements. For a pharmacist, the casual rate is:

$41.74 × 1.25 = **$52.18 per hour**

If you work 38 hours per week as a casual, your annual gross would be:

$52.18 × 38 × 52 = **$103,097.68**

Note: The award states that casual penalty rates (e.g., for evening or Saturday work) already include the casual loading. You should never add casual loading on top of a rate that already includes it. Use the [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) guide for more details.

### Superannuation

Superannuation is paid **on top** of your ordinary earnings. The current super guarantee rate is 12%, applied to your ordinary time earnings up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a full-time pharmacist earning $82,478:

$82,478 × 12% = **$9,897.39 in super**

Your total remuneration (salary plus super) would be about $92,375. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional cost to the employer. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more on how super interacts with salary.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross pay is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners).

For a pharmacist earning $82,478, the estimated tax (using the full tax-free threshold) is approximately $16,497, and Medicare is about $1,650, leaving a take-home pay of around **$64,331 per year** (or $1,237 per week). This is an estimate only; your actual tax may vary depending on deductions, HELP repayments, or the Medicare levy surcharge. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more detailed calculation.

## Important Distinctions

- **National Minimum Wage vs Award Rate**: The National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026), but the pharmacist award rate of $41.74 is much higher. Award rates always override the NMW for covered employees.
- **Full-Time vs Part-Time vs Casual**: Full-time and part-time employees receive the base hourly rate plus penalty rates where applicable. Casual employees get the 25% loading instead of paid leave.
- **Super is not included in the hourly rate**: It is paid on top of ordinary earnings, not on penalty rates or overtime.
- **Annualised wage arrangements**: Some pharmacists and pharmacy assistants level 4 can agree to an annualised wage that covers penalty rates and overtime, but it must be at least equal to what they would have earned under the award.

For a full list of award classifications and rates, refer to the [reference tables](/data) or the Fair Work Ombudsman’s pay guides.

## Summary

A **pharmacist salary Australia** under the award starts at $41.74 per hour, or $82,478 per year for a 38-hour week. Casual pharmacists earn $52.18 per hour including loading. Superannuation of 12% is paid on top, and tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident rates. Always check the latest award and use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to see how your rate translates to different pay periods.
